extracted.intended_audience: small business owners, founders, and in-house/outsourced PR or marketing people who need to write and distribute press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and formatting newsworthy press releases specifically tailored to small businesses — covering types of releases, structure, phrasing, distribution, and optional AI-assisted drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release length guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: The average press release is just a page long — two at most.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the release concise; long releases risk being ignored by journalists or not published. Be wary of boilerplate length because some outlets may not publish if it’s too long.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential press release structure/format
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic elements of a press release: company logo at the top, captivating title or headline, location (headquarters) and dateline, introduction, body (up to three paragraphs of details), bulleted facts (if you have any), boilerplate, contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting can vary (some place contact info before the boilerplate) but include all crucial elements. Use bulleted facts for digestibility when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know your audience
rubrics_metrics.description: To maximize impact, know your audience; your angle or perspective should interest readers and reflect your distribution channels and platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor words, expressions, and tone to the outlet’s readership. Create different versions for different types of readers or outlets. Research and pitch journalists who cover your niche — otherwise a newsworthy release may be useless in incompatible outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a captivating headline
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline should be eye-catching, reflect the purpose of the release, and convey value from the get-go.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific, make it short, utilize action verbs, and avoid giving everything away while still enticing the reader. Take time crafting headlines — a long or puzzling headline can turn the audience away.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a fascinating subtitle
rubrics_metrics.description: A one-sentence summary after the headline that gives a taste of what’s to come and encourages reading the whole release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every release uses a subtitle, but when done right it adds momentum and clarity without spelling out everything.

rubrics_metrics.name: First paragraph must provide key information (the W’s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your introduction or first paragraph should provide answers to the most important questions (where, what, when, who, and why).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many readers skim, so put essential facts up front. Use the second paragraph to establish credibility and support with statistics, research, or sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide valuable supporting information in the body
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsequent paragraphs should expand with relevant details, statistics, and context that support the purpose of the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include data, research, examples, and facts to strengthen the story. Use bulleted lists for clarity where helpful (e.g., product features, availability). Avoid burying the main details in long paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a quote from an authoritative source
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a quote to provide perspective and added value — best when from someone of authority in your company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes help shape the narrative and lend credibility. Don’t use random quotes; tailor quotes to the story. For some beats (e.g., sports), provide concise, 'twittable' quotes and statements from relevant individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add relevant background information
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer additional details that emphasize your point and support the overall narrative without putting key points at the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell short stories (e.g., how a merger happened) or briefly explain unfamiliar tools. Relate the release to relevant trends when appropriate, but keep it related and supportive of the main message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a strong boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: A short paragraph that functions as the company’s business card and should include a brief description of what you do, your industry, the company name, contact info and website, how long you've been in business, and any awards or accolades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the boilerplate concise; it helps journalists remember the brand and may be used verbatim in coverage. Watch the word count since overly long boilerplates may be excluded by outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include clear contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide contact information for journalists or media outlets so they can follow up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some formats place contact info before the boilerplate; either placement is acceptable as long as the contact details are present and easy to find.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use bulleted facts/lists when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Event releases and releases with key facts benefit from bulleted forms or lists so the 'what', 'where', and 'when' aren't buried in paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bulleted lists make critical details digestible and memorable for readers and newsrooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor content to the press release type
rubrics_metrics.description: Different types of releases (business launch, product launch, events, partnerships/mergers/acquisitions) require different emphases and content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Business launch — introduce team, credentials, personalize to brand tone; Product launch — be informational yet exciting, highlight specs, availability, pricing, benefits; Events — include key details and bulleted takeaways; Partnerships/mergers — explain why it happened, who benefits, and consider a separate release to introduce new leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product launch specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Product launch press releases should highlight product specifications, availability, pricing, and other relevant details to capture attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize benefits to customers (e.g., performance improvements), mention flavors/sizes or pre-order periods when relevant, and include bulleted lists of features to help readers and buyers decide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event press release best practice
rubrics_metrics.description: An event press release should maximize awareness, gain media coverage, and inform the public by including clear details of the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bullets for the 'what', 'where', and 'when'; include reasons attendees or press should care; tie to achievements or outcomes where relevant (e.g., training success rates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships/merger announcement guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: When announcing partnerships, mergers, or acquisitions include relevant info such as who is involved, why it happened, who benefits, and reputational details if permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name partner organizations and, if allowed, their notable clients to establish credibility. Consider whether to introduce new leaders in the same release or a separate announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness and angle selection
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no one-size-fits-all formula; choose an angle that makes the announcement newsworthy for the target outlets and audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An effective angle reflects audience interest and distribution channels. The unique selling proposition, community impact, or growth milestones can serve as key messages to craft the angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use statistics, research, and sources for credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Support claims with statistics, research, and other sources when relevant to establish credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistics can be placed within paragraphs or bulleted lists. For example, cite relevant figures to justify business-impact claims; ensure sources are reliable and accurately represented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt quotes and content to beat-specific needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Different types of journalists/beat coverage expect different formats (e.g., sports journalists want concise, 'twittable' quotes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt tone and length of quotes and content to the expectations of the outlet or beat to increase pickup chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create different versions for different audiences/outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies sometimes create different versions of a press release tailored for different types of readers or outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust tone, technical detail, and emphasis to match specialized trade publications vs. local media vs. general consumer press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid anti-patterns (unclear or long headlines, buried facts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid long, puzzling headlines and burying key details in long paragraphs, which can turn readers away or make the release ineffective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep headlines short and specific, lead with the W’s, and use bullets where necessary so important info is immediately visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release distribution timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing matters for distribution; internal analysis (Prowly’s) found Thursday is the best day to send press releases in their dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider day-of-week effects when scheduling distribution; consult distribution-service research for optimal sending times.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-assisted press release drafting workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: When using AI tools (like Prowly’s Press Release Generator): enter the type, pick a target audience, choose language, enter key messages (USP, community impact, growth), answer follow-up questions, customize and edit the draft, and use AI suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI will ask targeted follow-ups (e.g., 10 tailored questions), suggest journalist contacts based on keywords, and offer editing suggestions based on multiple internal criteria (page mentions an AI assistant reviews drafts against 11 key criteria). Customize headers, font styles, and length after generation; always manually review and tailor content before sending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key messages to provide when drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: Three example key messages to supply for generating a small business press release: Unique Selling Proposition (USP), Community Impact and Involvement, Growth and Success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be as specific as possible — clear USPs, examples of community involvement, and recent achievements/milestones help the draft and journalist interest. These messages help the AI or writer prioritize content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media targeting and journalist research
rubrics_metrics.description: Target journalists and news outlets relevant to the story — e.g., eCommerce journalists for Shopify coupon news — to increase pickup likelihood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use media databases and recommended contacts; research what a journalist has covered to tailor the pitch and reduce irrelevant outreach.
